original_question: Develop an infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory for spaces whose points code copies of a fixed homogeneous structure, extending Galvin-Prikry-style and Ellentuck-style theorems from [omega]^omega to spaces of copies and ideally recovering exact big Ramsey degrees in that setting.
target_in_paper: Problem 6.4 in Section 6: "Develop infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory on spaces of copies of a homogeneous structure," together with the immediately following paragraph explaining the intended Galvin–Prikry and Ellentuck analogies and the ideal of recovering exact big Ramsey degrees; for the meaning of that last clause, the relevant earlier references are Question 2.3(2) and Definition 2.4.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies that the relevant item is an open problem about infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory on spaces of copies of a homogeneous structure, not a general big-Ramsey-degree existence problem. It also accurately tracks the surrounding context in the paper: extending Galvin–Prikry- and Ellentuck-type theorems from [ω]^ω to spaces of copies, treating points as codes for copies of a fixed homogeneous structure, and aiming—ideally—to recover exact big Ramsey degrees in that framework.
missing_details: The ambient setting is a countably infinite homogeneous relational structure K (equivalently, the Fraïssé limit of its age), not an arbitrary coding space; in this paper, "homogeneous" means countably infinite homogeneous unless otherwise specified.
The intended copy-space is a subspace of [ω]^ω in which each infinite subset represents a copy of one fixed homogeneous structure K.

The Galvin–Prikry side of the analogy is specifically about Borel subsets of the copy-space, while the Ellentuck side is the optimal strengthening for sets with the property of Baire relative to a finer topology.
In the paper, the phrase about recovering exact big Ramsey degrees is not the formal statement of Problem 6.4 itself; it appears in the immediately following discussion as an ideal desideratum.

To make "recover exact big Ramsey degrees" stand alone in paper-faithful terms, one should say that the theorem should recover canonical partitions for copies of each finite A in Age(K), since Question 2.3(2) formulates exact big Ramsey degrees via canonical partitions.

The survey does not claim a general solution. It records only partial evidence: a Galvin–Prikry-style theorem for spaces of copies of the Rado graph is known, and the author reports work in progress for structures satisfying SDAP+ with relations of arity at most two. A refined question should therefore avoid sounding as if the general theory is already established.
refined_question: Fix a countably infinite homogeneous relational structure K, and represent the family of its copies by a subspace X_K ⊆ [ω]^ω whose elements code copies of K. Can one develop an infinite-dimensional Ramsey theory for X_K extending the Galvin–Prikry theorem and Ellentuck’s theorem—namely, for Borel subsets of X_K, and optimally for all subsets of X_K having the property of Baire in a suitable finer topology, can one pass to a subcopy K' ≅ K so that the induced subspace of codes for copies of K inside K' is either contained in or disjoint from the given set—in a form strong enough to recover the canonical partitions, and hence the exact big Ramsey degrees, of finite substructures A ∈ Age(K)?
justification: The closest official formulation in the paper is the single-sentence open problem labeled Problem 6.4. Your draft already includes the two pieces of nearby context that the paper itself immediately adds: first, the intended analogy with Galvin–Prikry and Ellentuck on [ω]^ω; second, Todorcevic’s desideratum that such an infinite-dimensional theorem should ideally recover exact big Ramsey degrees. The only substantial sharpening needed is to make explicit the paper's ambient setting (countable homogeneous relational structures), the model of the copy-space as a subspace of [ω]^ω, the Borel/property-of-Baire split corresponding to Galvin–Prikry versus Ellentuck, and the paper-specific meaning of "exact big Ramsey degrees" via canonical partitions from Question 2.3(2) and Definition 2.4. Since the paper presents this as an open problem and only mentions partial progress for the Rado graph and for SDAP+ structures of arity at most two, the refined question should stay at that level and not broaden into a general theory beyond the survey's stated intent.
